title: Safety Moment: Test what you disturb (Gas terminal release and fire, 2020)
audience: Session leaders (T2): maintenance and shift supervisors and trainers running a ten-minute session for maintenance and instrument crews (T1)
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Derived from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; learnings are evidence-linked but should be validated by the organisation before adoption. Draft learnings: the investigation status is in progress.

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate every item before the session.

bottom_line.text: No specification, no fit: a seal that does not match the original is a change, not a spare.
A joint you opened is not proven until it has passed a recorded test to the written test pressure.
When the same fault comes back, say so on the job record; a repeat is a warning, not a routine job.

items.text: On 18 Sep 2020 the seal on a 1986 condensate meter at the gas terminal was changed. The maker's specification had been lost, so a locally bought round O-ring was fitted, as had become regular practice, and the system was brought only to operating pressure, with no test to design pressure [FND-8C0BB623; FND-212DC9B7; EVD-8645; EVD-2894]. The meter went back on line the next day and was in use on 24 Sep, when that seal was the probable source of a release that later caught fire [FND-15279F97; EVD-2894].
The meter was built for a rectangular-slot gasket; the round O-ring was a local substitute, bought with no specification or quality check [FND-7A32AC87; EVD-8645].

This was the third seal change on the same meter in about 22 months, and a malfunction notification had been raised the day before the last one. None of the repeats led to a review of why it kept leaking [FND-69067A1C; FND-82FC718D; EVD-1494; EVD-0591].
No written procedure covered testing these high-pressure meters before they went back into service, so holding at operating pressure became the normal check [FND-257C1100; EVD-2894].
Check the part against the groove and the specification before you fit it. If nobody can show a specification, stop and ask the supervisor.
items.when: before fitting a seal or gasket on a pressure part

items.text: Before you hand the equipment back, ask for the written test pressure and the witness, and write the test result on the job record; if no test was done, write that.
Write "repeat failure" on the job record when you fix the same fault again, and tell the supervisor how often you have seen it.

items.question: Which pressure parts on our unit have no specification we can find?
items.why: The seal on this meter had no specification on file, so a substitute became the normal part [FND-B356F15B; EVD-8645].
items.answer: A good answer names the parts, where their specification should be kept, and who the crew asks when a spare differs from the original.

items.question: What test proves a joint we have just made, and where is the result written?
items.why: After the seal change the system was only brought to operating pressure, with no test to design pressure [FND-7C5ED5B3; EVD-2894].
items.answer: A good answer gives the test, the test pressure, who witnesses it and where the result is recorded before operations accept the equipment.

items.question: Which items do we keep fixing, and who decides whether we repair again or look for the cause?
items.why: Repeat seal failures on this meter were handled as routine repairs [FND-82FC718D; EVD-1494].
items.answer: A good answer names the items, says where a repeat would show on the job record, and names the role that starts a cause review.

items.title: Test what you disturb
items.purpose: A one-minute clip to open the session before the questions.

segments.visual: A metering skid, and an old meter with its retaining plate off.
segments.narration: This condensate meter dated from 1986. Its seal had been changed three times in under two years.

segments.visual: A round O-ring held next to a rectangular groove.
segments.narration: The maker's specification was lost, so a locally bought O-ring was fitted, as usual.

segments.visual: A pressure gauge rising to its normal operating mark and stopping there.
segments.narration: The joint was held at operating pressure and handed back. It was never tested to design pressure.

segments.visual: A crew member writes a test result on a job record and shows it to the supervisor.
segments.narration: Six days later that seal was the probable source of a release that caught fire. Before you hand back, ask for the test.

limits: This session is built from the frontline Learning Cards for LR-01, LR-02 and LR-05 and uses the same story; the cards are what the crew keep afterwards.

The organisation's fixes (re-establishing the specification, a return-to-service procedure, a repeat-failure trigger) are for supervisor-coach and manager-coach; they are mentioned here only so crews recognise the trap.
